LCA of various H /NG blending pathways: ANL will develop the various H /NG blends 2 2 pathways in the Greenhouse gases, Regulated Emissions, and Energy use in Technologies (GREET) model using the energy and emissions inventory data from Subtasks 1.1–1.3 to conduct a thorough LCA with respect to important metrics such as energy use, GHG emissions, and CAP emissions. The results of the various pathways will be compared to the conventional and shale gas pathways. From the LCA, key environmental performance parameters will be identified and evaluated using uncertainty and stochastic analyses. The LCA will be combined with the TEA by NREL so that the life cycle carbon intensity reduction by various H /NG blends compared to baseline conventional NG pathways will be 2 used with the levelized cost of the NG/H blend to calculate the abatement cost of CO while 2 2 also considering the impacts of possible GHG credits under various existing and hypothetical low-carbon fuel frameworks. Subtask 3.2: Analysis of Synthetic Methane Production from CO + H as an Alternative to 2 2 Blending H With NG – Description 2 While blending H with NG can leverage existing NG infrastructure and thus eliminate the need 2 to build costly infrastructure dedicated to H delivery, such blending will likely incur costs 2 downstream of the blending point, depending on the blending ratio. These include possible costs associated with modifying NG infrastructure components (e.g., pipeline coating, storage, compressors, engines driving compressors, leak detection, and safety devices), as well as possible costs associated with modifying end-use equipment (e.g., burner designs, heat exchangers, NO mitigation). An alternative approach to using clean H to reduce the carbon x 2 intensity of conventional NG is to use H with CO to synthesize methane, which can be injected 2 2 into existing NG pipelines while being fully compatible with existing NG infrastructure components and end-use applications. While this synthetic NG production scenario eliminates all downstream costs associated with the H blending alternative, there is additional cost associated 2 with the synthesis of methane (e.g., CO capture and purification, CO compression and 2 2 transmission, in addition to the synthesis process). However, the synthesis process has a carbon conversion ratio >95% and energy efficiency >80%, while also producing high-quality heat (approximately 300C, due to the exothermic reaction of CO + H ), which can be used for 2 2 building or industrial heating applications. Furthermore, the synthetic natural gas (SNG) alternative can use an unlimited and varying amount of H production with no impact on 2 downstream processes. Additionally, the SNG pathway avoids the dilemma of a H blending 2 scenario created by the much lower volumetric energy density of an H compared to CH . 2 4 19 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications.
